data.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
data.description:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) announced Monday, November 23, that it had reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and a director. The board voted unanimously, and Nvidia’s SEC filing dates the decision to Sunday, November 22. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, remains chief financial officer. Harvey C. Jones remains board chair.

The decision reverses the position Nvidia set out on its November 17 earnings call, when it said the board did not intend to bring Huang back. Directors said they met with Huang and received input from senior U.S. officials. The board said that input gave it confidence that his return posed no national security risk. President Donald Trump had publicly called for Huang’s return Sunday, the Associated Press reported.

Nvidia said its independent board investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will continue. The company also began looking for a chief compliance officer who will report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. Nvidia said it would continue cooperating with government investigations and inquiries.

Nvidia shares rose nearly 30% in early U.S. regular-session trading Monday, Reuters reported. The stock was already higher before the announcement, as the Digest’s premarket briefing recorded. The decision comes less than two weeks after Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation.

data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.

data.title: What Is the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA)? A Complete Guide
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), often referred to as the Dow Jones, the Dow 30, or simply the Dow, is one of the world’s most recognized stock market indexes. The DJIA tracks 30 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, making it a widely followed indicator of the overall health of the U.S. economy and stock market. Investors searching for DJIA today, DJIA futures, or Dow Jones price updates often turn to this index as a barometer of market sentiment.

But what exactly is the DJIA, what stocks does it include, and how do traders and long-term investors use it in their strategies?

What Is the DJIA?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a price-weighted index created in 1896 by Charles Dow and Edward Jones. Unlike market-cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, the DJIA assigns weight based on a stock’s price rather than its market capitalization. This means a company with a higher stock price (e.g., Apple or UnitedHealth) influences the index more heavily than lower-priced stocks.

The DJIA is designed to reflect the performance of blue-chip companies across different sectors of the U.S. economy. It does not include utilities or transportation stocks, which are tracked by separate Dow indexes.

What Companies Are in the DJIA?

The DJIA is composed of 30 large, publicly traded U.S. companies that are considered leaders in their industries. These companies span sectors such as technology, finance, healthcare, consumer goods, and industrials.

Here’s a snapshot of the DJIA holdings (as of 2025, September 15th):

Note: The index is reviewed periodically, and constituents may change depending on mergers, bankruptcies, or shifts in market relevance.

How Does the DJIA Work?

  • Price-Weighted Methodology: Higher-priced stocks have more influence.
  • Dow Divisor: A proprietary number adjusted for stock splits, dividends, and corporate actions ensures continuity.
  • Sector Balance: While tech stocks (Apple, Microsoft) now hold significant weight, the index aims to represent the broader U.S. economy.

If Apple (AAPL) rises $5 in a day, it has the same impact on the DJIA as Boeing (BA) rising $5, even though their market caps differ drastically.

Why Do Investors Watch the DJIA?

  • Economic Barometer: The DJIA today is seen as a snapshot of the U.S. economy.
  • Historical Importance: Created in 1896, it has over 125 years of market history.
  • Market Sentiment: Widely quoted on news outlets and financial platforms.
  • Trading Opportunities: Investors follow DJIA futures, DJIA ETFs, and Dow Jones index funds for exposure.

How to Trade or Invest in the DJIA

Investors can’t buy the DJIA directly but can gain exposure through exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures contracts, or mutual funds:

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) – tracks the DJIA closely.
  • DJIA Futures – contracts traded on CME, allowing leveraged exposure.
  • Index Funds – designed for long-term buy-and-hold investors.

data.title: VNET Revenue Rises 15% as Wholesale Data Centers Lead Growth
data.description:
VNET Group (NASDAQ: VNET) reported on November 23 that third-quarter revenue rose 14.8% to 2.96 billion yuan ($442 million). The China-based data-center operator’s earnings release showed wholesale sales up 27.6% to 1.22 billion yuan, accounting for about 41% of total revenue.

The quarter ended September 30. Wholesale data-center capacity in service rose 44.1% from a year earlier to 1,127 megawatts, while capacity in use by customers rose 37.1% to 797 megawatts. VNET said it booked a 60-megawatt order from a cloud provider it did not name. Retail data-center revenue grew 5.1%.

The cost of expanding capacity showed up in gross profit, which fell 13.4% to 466.9 million yuan. VNET cited higher depreciation and rising utility costs relative to revenue. Its SEC filing showed the net loss attributable to VNET narrowing to 83.1 million yuan from 307.0 million yuan a year earlier, helped by a change in the fair value of financial instruments. Excluding such changes, it reported an adjusted net loss of 46.6 million yuan after an adjusted profit of 61.9 million yuan a year earlier.

Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP earnings measure, rose 21.7% to 923.1 million yuan, above the estimate cited by Investing.com. VNET kept its 2026 revenue forecast at 11.5 billion to 11.8 billion yuan and its adjusted EBITDA range at 3.55 billion to 3.75 billion yuan. It now expects capital expenditures of 8 billion to 10 billion yuan for the year.

data.title: Texas Pacific Land to Buy EagleRock in $3 Billion Permian Deal
data.description:
Texas Pacific Land (NYSE: TPL) said on November 23 it would buy EagleRock Land (NYSE: EROK) in an all-stock transaction with an implied equity value of about $3 billion. The joint announcement said the combined company would own about one million surface acres and expand its water business across the Permian Basin.

EagleRock Class A shareholders would receive 0.0831 shares in the new holding company for each share they own. That worked out to about $23.56 per EagleRock share using Texas Pacific Land’s five-day volume-weighted average share price through November 20, Investing.com reported. Existing Texas Pacific Land shareholders would receive one new share for each share they own and hold about 86% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis.

The deal adds roughly 59,000 acres of owned land, mostly in Lea County, New Mexico, and expands Texas Pacific Land’s presence in the Midland Basin. The companies estimate that the combination would lift capacity for non-potable water sourcing and treatment of water brought to the surface during oil and gas production by 49%, to about 1.5 million barrels per day.

The companies expect to close in the first half of 2027 after EagleRock shareholders vote and the federal antitrust waiting period expires or ends. Shareholders representing more than half of EagleRock’s voting power have agreed to support the transaction.

data.title: CrowdStrike Agrees to Buy Zscaler in $43.9 Billion Stock Deal
data.description:
CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) agreed on November 23 to buy Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) in an all-stock deal with an enterprise value of about $43.9 billion. Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders would receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share they own.

Using CrowdStrike’s November 20 closing price, the exchange ratio valued each Zscaler share at $260.41, about 34% above Zscaler’s close that day. Because the ratio is fixed, the dollar value of the consideration moves with CrowdStrike’s shares. Current Zscaler shareholders would own about 15.9% of the combined company.

The acquisition would bring Zscaler’s cloud-based network protections into CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform. CrowdStrike is best known for protecting devices such as laptops and desktops, while Zscaler focuses on how users connect to applications and data, the Associated Press reported. The companies already work with some of the same customers, giving CrowdStrike an opportunity to sell a broader set of services through one platform.

CrowdStrike expects annualized cost savings to reach $500 million within 18 to 24 months of closing, largely from combining data-center infrastructure, vendor contracts and operations. The company is targeting the second half of its fiscal 2028 for closing, subject to Zscaler shareholder approval and regulatory clearances. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry is expected to continue leading that business and join CrowdStrike’s board.

data.title: Stock Futures Rebound as Nvidia Bounces; PCE and GDP Await in Thanksgiving Week
data.description:
U.S. stock futures rebounded sharply before the open on Monday, November 23, as technology shares recovered part of last week's losses. The move follows the Dow's and Nasdaq's worst weeks since 2020, leaving all three major U.S. indexes in correction territory. Wednesday's inflation and growth reports now provide the main macroeconomic test in a trading week shortened by Thanksgiving.

At about 5:41 a.m. ET Monday, delayed CNBC quotes showed December S&P 500 futures up 2.77%, Nasdaq-100 futures up 3.47% and Dow futures up 1.99%. In today’s pre-market video briefing, we examine the rebound, Nvidia's weekend news and the Asian selloff. These refreshed readings differ slightly from those at the time of recording.

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) traded at $136.09 at 5:51 a.m. ET Monday, up 8.41% in premarket trading, according to CNBC quotes. President Donald Trump said Sunday that he hoped its board would rehire Jensen Huang. The board said last week it had no plans to reinstate him. Huang resigned on November 12, and finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO, CNBC reported.

The bounce follows Nvidia's 14.01% decline to $125.53 at Friday's November 20 regular-session close. Reuters reported that the SEC was examining potential accounting issues; an inquiry does not establish wrongdoing. Nvidia also completed its seventh consecutive weekly loss, its longest such streak since 2008. The broader damage was substantial: the S&P 500 lost 8.6% last week, the Nasdaq about 10% and the Dow 8%. Our Friday closing recap covers the selloff, which extended beyond technology. Monday's futures gains alone do not establish that the correction has ended.

Asia offered a mixed backdrop. South Korea's Kospi closed Monday down 3.31% at 4,708.54, while Japan was closed for a public holiday, according to CNBC. South Korean officials agreed at an emergency meeting Sunday to prepare for possible deployment of a market stabilization fund. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said Monday that the timing and size would depend on conditions, the Korea Times reported. Preparations do not mean the fund has begun buying shares.

The BEA schedule puts October personal income and outlays, including PCE inflation, and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP at 8:30 a.m. ET Wednesday, November 25. Those releases precede the Fed's December 8–9 policy meeting. Fed Governor Lisa Cook warned Friday that delaying rate increases could leave policymakers behind the curve, CNBC reported. The rebound therefore arrives with inflation and interest-rate uncertainty still unresolved.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise reports after Monday's close; Dell and Workday follow after Tuesday's close, with Best Buy due before Tuesday's opening bell, according to CNBC's earnings calendar. These results bring fresh evidence on hardware, business software and consumer demand. Our Thanksgiving-week preview sets out the broader calendar. U.S. stock markets are closed Thursday, November 26, and close at 1 p.m. ET Friday, November 27.

data.title: October Inflation and Retail Earnings Lead a Short Thanksgiving Trading Week
data.description:
U.S. investors get a new reading on inflation and household spending on Wednesday, November 25, before Thanksgiving shortens the trading week. The releases follow a week in which the S&P 500 fell 8.6% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 10.0% through Friday’s close. The Digest’s closing recap detailed the sell-off in chip and other AI-related stocks.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis will release October personal income and outlays at 8:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday. The report includes the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure, the personal consumption expenditures price index. In September, that index rose 3.6% from a year earlier. Core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 3.1%. Spending increased 0.5% from August in dollar terms and less than 0.1% after adjusting for inflation.

The Federal Reserve’s calendar puts the Beige Book at 2 p.m. ET the same day. The report draws on interviews and other accounts across Fed districts. Together the releases add data on prices and regional business conditions before the Fed’s December 8–9 policy meeting, when officials are due to update their economic projections.

Best Buy (NYSE: BBY) has its fiscal third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday at 8 a.m. ET. The electronics retailer projected comparable sales growth of 1% to 3% in August, following a 4.1% increase in its second quarter. Its results offer an early look at demand for electronics ahead of the busiest shopping days. Reuters reported that the strength of holiday spending is in focus after the sell-off in tech shares.

Under the NYSE holiday schedule, the stock market is closed Thursday, November 26, and the regular session ends at 1 p.m. ET on Friday, November 27.

data.title: EU and Indonesia Sign Trade Deal to Cut Duties on Nearly All Goods
data.description:
The European Union and Indonesia signed a trade pact and a separate investment protection agreement in Brussels on Saturday, November 21. The European Commission said the trade deal would remove duties on 98.5% of tariff lines once implemented and save EU exporters more than €600 million a year in customs duties. The bloc and Indonesia traded €28.9 billion in goods in 2025.

Cars are one example of how the deal could change costs for exporters. Indonesia’s duties on European vehicle imports can reach 50%, Reuters reported. The pact would remove those barriers over time. It would also let EU companies operate with full ownership in parts of Indonesia’s services market, including computer services and telecommunications.

The investment pact addresses how investors are treated once they enter a market. It sets protections against discriminatory treatment and expropriation for investors on both sides. The Commission identified electric vehicles, electronics and pharmaceuticals as areas where the broader package could expand investment opportunities.

The European Parliament must still consent, and Indonesia is completing its own ratification procedures. The Commission expects provisional application in early 2027. The timing matters for Indonesian exporters because they are due to lose preferential tariffs under a separate EU program on January 1, according to the Council of the EU.

data.title: S&P 500 Enters Correction and Nasdaq Falls 5.3% as Chip Stocks Slide
data.description:
U.S. stocks ended Friday, November 20, with the S&P 500 in correction territory and the Nasdaq Composite down for the year. At the 4 p.m. ET close, the S&P 500 was down 3.7% at 6,910.39 and the Nasdaq was down 5.3% at 22,617.73. The Dow reversed an early gain to finish 949.73 points lower at 48,147.33, a 1.9% drop.

The S&P 500 finished more than 10% below its October 6 record, the threshold commonly used to define a correction. Friday was its seventh straight loss. For the week, the S&P 500 shed 8.6%, the Nasdaq lost 10.0% and the Russell 2000 index of smaller companies fell 7.5%, according to Associated Press closing data. The Nasdaq ended 2.7% below its 2025 close.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 10.7%. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) lost about 14%. Its shares were already down more than 6% before Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues, citing two people briefed on the matter. Reuters said the scope and start date of the inquiry were unclear and that the SEC declined to comment.

Anthropic was another weak spot, closing its second session down 9.1% at $88.30, still above its $83 offer price. The morning briefing tracked the pressure on AI shares after the company’s debut. By Friday’s close, the losses had extended to smaller companies as well, with the Russell 2000 down 2.8% for the session.

In bonds, the Treasury’s 10-year benchmark yield fell to 4.92% from 5.04% on Thursday as Treasury prices rose. The University of Michigan’s final November reading showed consumer sentiment rising to 51.5 from 48.0 in October. The interviews ended Monday, before the sharp losses at the end of the week.

The next trading week is shortened for Thanksgiving. The NYSE calendar shows markets closed Thursday, November 26, and a 1 p.m. ET close Friday, November 27.
